Agriculture | Representative Tracey Mann Skip to main content Agriculture Image Agriculture is the heartbeat of the Big First District and America. The Big First ranks number one in congressional districts in wheat, beef, and sorghum production. As a proud fifth-generation Kansan who grew up working thousands of hours on my family ’s farm south of Quinter, I am honored to represent farmers, ranchers, and agricultural producers on the House Agriculture Committee and in Congress. The distance from farm to fork has never been wider, and there are fewer and fewer legislators that have experience on the farm. I proudly serve on the House Agriculture Committee  as Chairman of the Subcommittee on Livestock, Dairy, and Poultry, and on the Subcommittee on Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development, and the Subcommittee on Nutrition, Foreign Agriculture, and Horticulture. As the Congressman for the Big First, I am hyper-focused on crop insurance, oversight, trade , and trade promotion when reauthorizing the next Farm Bill. We need strong agricultural policy that address es the challenges and changes agricultural producers are currently facing. American farmers, ranchers, and agricultural producers deserve it, America’s food and national security depend on it, and Congress must deliver it. I am committed to working with my colleagues on legislation that both puts the needs of the First District at the forefront of policy and honors those who feed, fuel, and clothe the world. Health Care | Representative Tracey Mann Skip to main content Health Care Image All Kansans should have access to affordable, quality, and accessible health care. I believe that health care should not be a one-size-fits-all policy, and I am committed to ensuring flexibility in the health care system so that Kansans can receive the care that they deserve. The Big First is unique; we have more critical access hospitals than any other Congressional district in the country. Critical access hospitals and 340-B programs are essential safety nets that provide health care options for rural communities while keeping costs down. I recognize that the high cost of prescription drugs is putting a strain on many Kansans' wallets, which is why I favor supporting programs such as 340-B. Additionally, I will continue to advocate for increased use of telehealth services, so that our rural communities have access to high-quality health care.   More on Health Care Image We can solve America’s rural health care crisis December 10, 2025 In The News Washington Times Every American should have access to quality, affordable health care regardless of their zip code. The 66 million Americans who call rural America home are no exception. Over the past two decades, there has been a growing health care crisis in rural America, and Washington, D.C. has been slow in adequately addressing the problem. They add brick and mortar to the values that make our country unique—freedom, self-determination, and the pursuit of happiness.
